references.text: Isaiah prophesies that the Lord's Spirit will rest upon the Messiah – [ref:Jes 11:2|Isaiah 11:2] points forward to what John the Baptist testifies: that the Spirit came down and remained on Jesus.
In [ref:Jes 42:1|Isaiah 42:1] God says about his servant: "I have put my Spirit upon him." This corresponds to the sign John received – that the Spirit would come down and remain on the chosen one.

[ref:Jes 61:1|Isaiah 61:1] speaks of the Lord's Spirit being upon the anointed one – a messianic prophecy which Jesus himself applied to himself (cf. [ref:Luk 4:18|Luke 4:18]), and which aligns with the coming of the Spirit upon him at his baptism.

In [ref:Joel 3:1|Joel 2:28] God promises to pour out his Spirit on all people – a prophecy fulfilled on the day of Pentecost (cf. [ref:Apg 2:17|Acts 2:17]) and connected with Jesus' role as the one who baptizes with the Holy Spirit.

In [ref:Matt 3:11|Matthew 3:11] John the Baptist says that he baptizes with water, but the one coming after him will baptize with the Holy Spirit and fire – a direct parallel to the statement that Jesus is the one who baptizes with the Spirit.
[ref:Matt 3:16|Matthew 3:16] describes Jesus' baptism where God's Spirit descends like a dove and comes upon him, fulfilling the sign God had given John the Baptist.
[ref:Mark 1:8|Mark 1:8] records John the Baptist's words that he himself baptizes with water, but Jesus will baptize with the Holy Spirit – the same contrast between water baptism and Spirit baptism.
In [ref:Mark 1:10|Mark 1:10] Jesus sees the Spirit come down upon him like a dove as he rises from the water – Mark's account of the sign John testified about.
[ref:Luk 3:16|Luke 3:16] is Luke's parallel where John the Baptist declares that the one coming after him will baptize with the Holy Spirit and fire.
[ref:Luk 3:22|Luke 3:22] tells how the Holy Spirit came down upon Jesus in bodily form like a dove – Luke's version of the visible coming of the Spirit upon Jesus.

[ref:Joh 15:26|John 15:26] speaks of the Advocate, the Spirit of truth, who proceeds from the Father and whom Jesus will send – Jesus as the one who gives the Spirit, just as John the Baptist testified.
In [ref:Joh 20:22|John 20:22] Jesus breathes on the disciples and says "Receive the Holy Spirit" – a concrete fulfillment that Jesus is the one who baptizes with the Holy Spirit.
[ref:Apg 1:5|Acts 1:5] repeats the contrast: John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit – Jesus' own words confirming John the Baptist's testimony.
[ref:Apg 2:4|Acts 2:4] describes Pentecost when all were filled with the Holy Spirit – the actual fulfillment of the promise that Jesus would baptize with the Spirit.

In [ref:Apg 11:16|Acts 11:16] Peter recalls the Lord's words that John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit – yet another confirmation of John the Baptist's testimony in John 1:33.

[ref:Tit 3:5-6|Titus 3:5-6] speaks of the renewing bath of the Holy Spirit, which God has poured out richly on us through Jesus Christ – this links the gift of the Spirit to the work of Jesus, in line with Jesus being the one who baptizes with the Spirit.
